steps.title: You're right
steps.say: Yes, in northern summer Earth is actually a bit farther from the Sun, in early July. So distance can't be the cause.

ops.text:
Yes! In July Earth is farther from the Sun,
yet the north is hot. Distance isn't the cause.

steps.title: The distance gap is tiny
steps.say: Earth's distance changes by only about 3 percent over the year, which is too small to make summer and winter.

ops.text: Distance changes only ~3% in a year.

steps.title: Clear the picture
steps.say: Let me clear the extra Earths and keep one on each side to compare the two seasons.

steps.title: Tilt toward the Sun
steps.say: In July the northern half tips toward the Sun, so sunlight hits it more directly and the days are longer.

ops.text:
July: north tilts
toward the Sun

steps.title: Tilt away from the Sun
steps.say: In January the north tips away, so the light is slanted and weaker, and the days are shorter. That is winter.

ops.text:
January: north tilts
away from the Sun

steps.title: The takeaway
steps.say: So seasons come from the tilt, which changes how direct the sunlight is, and not from distance.
